transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Samir Das (Redwood AE), Elena Park (Redwood SE), Ravi Menon (Redwood CSM); Priya Shah (Acme SRE), Carlos Martinez (Acme Infra), Lena Wu (Acme Security), Tom Reynolds (Acme Product)

Summary: quick follow-up to last week's outage where Acme saw elevated token latencies and memory OOMs on Redwood Dedicated nodes; review of RCA, mitigations implemented, next steps for reliability improvements and gating for Reserved Capacity contract.

Topics: incident timeline, autoscaling behaviors, KV cache invalidation, pre-warm strategies, observability gaps, security questions (KMS/audit logs), next steps and deliverables.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we wanted to run through the postmortem follow up, confirm what went wrong, what we've already done and the action items. sorry for the slightly long agenda, we'll be concise.
[00:18] Priya (Acme): yep thanks, last Friday around 02:10 UTC we saw a spike in 95th pct latency and then within 10 minutes CPU and memory climbed on two pods and one node hit OOM, autoscaler didn't bring up new nodes quick enough - we ended up failing over to Hosted as a fallback.
[00:37] Elena (Redwood): yes, from our side we correlate that to a combination of a sudden shift in sequence lengths in the workload and some cache invalidation events. the KV cache population dropped due to a bug in one of the model routing headers so requests stopped hitting the cached paths, which caused higher compute.
[00:58] Carlos (Acme): to add, we also had a maintenance window on our cloud provider so our spot capacity was reduced; HPA thresholds were tuned quite aggressively to save cost, so it was a perfect storm.
[01:15] Samir: right, and to be clear, there were two separate failure modes: 1) request-level cost spike from losing prefix/KV cache hits, 2) kube scaling lag because of pod density + quota. both converged.
[01:32] Tom (Acme): can you explain the KV cash - i mean cache - explanation again? some of the product folks were confused.
[01:40] Elena: sure, so our runtime maintains a KV cache for prefixes and for common prompts, when that's warmed you get 30-60% less GPU compute per token. in this incident, a header mutation from the edge sent requests to a slightly different model route which bypassed the existing cache shards; cache miss rate spiked from ~12% to ~87% in under 3 minutes. transcription: "KV cash" shows up in the logs too haha.
[02:05] Priya: ok that explains the compute jump. on autoscaling, our HPA was capped and the nodegroup autoscaler had a 5-minute cool-down due to our provider settings, not Redwood - so we had to failover.
[02:22] Ravi (Redwood CSM): thanks for that context, and sorry again for the impact. we did implement a couple of mitigations: immediate config patch to make routing header tolerant, a hotfix to recover some cache shards, and we added a temporary lower OOM threshold on the nodes to trigger earlier restarts while we investigate.
[02:44] Lena (Acme Security): quick sec, on the hotfix - does that change any KMS or key usage? we need to know for compliance.
[02:52] Elena: no, the hotfix was purely routing/sidecar and cache behavior; we didn't touch KMS or key handling. audit logs remain intact; we'll attach the audit range to the postmortem doc.
[03:07] Samir: also important: we pushed a traffic routing fallback so when a model variant is missing a warmed cache we route to compatible variant on hosted tier automatically. this is already enabled for the Acme prod env as of 09:30 UTC yesterday.
[03:22] Carlos: is that going to raise costs since it goes to hosted?
[03:27] Samir: it can for the short term; we're monitoring and it should only be triggered during degraded states. we can add a policy to prefer cheaper quantized variants first.
[03:38] Tom: what about longer-term reliability changes?
[03:41] Elena: we recommend three engineering items: 1) pre-warm key cache shards during deploys (pre-warm logic), 2) synthetic canaries that exercise long-sequence prompts every 5 minutes to detect seq-length distribution shifts, 3) revise autoscaler policies and node pool quotas - consider reserved capacity for peak tails.
[04:00] Priya: synthetic canaries sound good - can Redwood provide a suggested set of prompts?
[04:05] Samir: yes, Elena will share a starter prompt set and a benchmark harness.
[04:10] Elena: note on quantization: for your workload the 4-bit quantized variant does increase CPU intensity in some kernels; we'll include model variant perf profiles so you can pick latency vs cost tradeoffs. there may be kernel mismatch on one specific transformer op on your older GPU node image - that was showing higher mem on the traces.
[04:35] Carlos: that might be our node image, we are running an older AMI. we can schedule an image upgrade but want to understand breaking changes.
[04:44] Samir: we'll provide a compatibility matrix - it's in the postmortem doc - and Elena will flag the risky kernels.
[04:52] Lena: security-wise, one ask: can you confirm TLS termination points and whether any logs contain PII during traces? we need to make sure nothing is stored unencrypted.
[05:02] Elena: all logs are encrypted in transit; we only capture trace IDs and anonymized aggregates. raw request bodies are not stored by default in our Hosted mode, but for Dedicated we respect the customer's retention and we can configure excluding payloads. we'll attach a doc on audit log shapes.
[05:22] Tom: ok, timeline wise what are the immediate deliverables?
[05:26] Samir: short list: postmortem doc with timeline and logs (Samir), benchmark results and canary prompts (Elena), your infra config (Acme), and a suggested reserved capacity plan & pricing option (Samir) - we'll aim to get pricing for reserved nodes after we see the benchmark.
[05:45] Priya: when will you run the benchmark? we want to see dedicated node numbers vs shared hosted fallback.
[05:50] Elena: we'll run both. plan: run dedicated-node bench on our staging cluster with similar AMI (if you can share AMI id) and run hosted fallback sim. results by 2026-11-24.
[06:04] Carlos: also, alerting gaps - we didn't have a synthetic that would have caught the prefix miss. can Redwood emit a specific metric for 'kv_cache_hit_rate' at 1-min resolution?
[06:14] Elena: yes, we can add that metric; we'll add it to the per-route dashboards.
[06:19] Ravi: ok. any blockers?
[06:22] Priya: we need the postmortem and the audit slice for our compliance team.
[06:25] Samir: will do.
[06:28] Tom: about reserved capacity - is there a trial or pilot we can run before committing?
[06:31] Samir: yes, we offer a 30-day pilot for Dedicated with a small reserved pool and a rollback to hosted; we'll include terms in the proposal.
[06:40] Priya: one more question on runbooks - could Redwood help with an SRE runbook for playbooks when cache miss spikes occur?
[06:46] Elena: yes, we can draft an SRE playbook and include run-commands and PoC scripts for cache warmers and traffic reroutes.
[06:55] Carlos: thanks, that would be helpful.
[06:58] Samir: recap of action items and owners, and dates in notes - we'll follow up via email and attach the postmortem links.
[07:06] Ravi: ok, any risks we should call out right now?
[07:09] Elena: residual kernel mismatch on older AMIs; if you can't upgrade we'll recommend node-level isolation for affected models.
[07:16] Lena: and security: we need to validate audit logs export for our compliance, but sounds promising.
[07:21] Samir: great, thanks everyone, we'll target those deliverables and reconvene after the benchmark.
[07:27] Priya: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
